## Situational notes from the rule notes

Every sentence below is copied from a rule's own note (the rule id is in front of it) and mentions a situation the rule exists for. Rest, food and drink rules are left out here; their items are in the band table above.

The spec's own guide page names it (line 229); the item and its aura or enchant id are read from the DB (docs/research/db-queries/tkbplay-205.result.txt).

The spec's own guide page names it (line 229); the item and its aura or enchant id are read from the DB (docs/research/db-queries/tkbplay-205.result.txt).

The spec guide page names it (warlock/demonology.md line 229).
- **WD00c-unending-breath-pre-swim — Unending Breath:** HO-TKB-PLAY-144 (round 131 BFD-C, p4-pioneer water.py: party uptime submerged 77.6%, the shaman's 18 Water Breathing casts spread 4/4/4/3/3 with 4 on a druid already in Aquatic Form while the mage was covered 35.6% of her time underwater): at a swim stretch (party.swim_ahead, p4-group 343) every member enters with at least five minutes of Unending Breath: a buff placed for an earlier stretch ran out in the next one.
- **WD00b-unending-breath — Unending Breath:** HO-TKB-PLAY-144 (round 131 BFD-C, p4-pioneer water.py: party uptime submerged 77.6%, the shaman's 18 Water Breathing casts spread 4/4/4/3/3 with 4 on a druid already in Aquatic Form while the mage was covered 35.6% of her time underwater): covered_by [131, 1066] (v30): a member in Aquatic Form or carrying the other breath buff is skipped. HO-TKB-PLAY-139 (owner, 2026-10-08: the party's shaman or warlock buffs every member before a swim and refreshes it while the party is underwater; druids use Aquatic Form for their own swims): Unending Breath (5697, instant, 10 min, 30 yd) on every member, the resident included, who lacks it or has under two minutes left (party_missing with refresh_below_ms, v28), while the party walks or holds at a swim stretch (party.swim_ahead, p4-group 343) or any member is submerged; in combat too, since a buff running out mid-fight underwater is how a member drowns.
- **WD0G1-demon-gate-felguard — Demon Gate:** HO-TKB-PLAY-276 (amp-3 draft rot-mage-warlock.patch of 2026-10-18, rebased by tkb-play onto main with HO-270..274; the amp-3 text follows): THE SPEC'S CORE AND A RULE NO FILE HAD: "no greater demon is ever summoned" was the first gap of the demonology audit (spec audit 2026-10-18, gap demo-1; `grep -rn "Infernal\|Felguard\|Doomguard\|Demon Gate\|Ritual of Doom" warlock/*/rotation.yaml` found nothing outside notes, while Power Overwhelming (WD03) sat there with no demon worth using it on). The guide's before-the-pull list opens with it: "Summon the greater demon for this boss ...
- **WD0G2-ritual-of-doom — Ritual of Doom:** HO-TKB-PLAY-276 (amp-3 draft rot-mage-warlock.patch of 2026-10-18, rebased by tkb-play onto main with HO-270..274; the amp-3 text follows): The Doomguard, same pre-boss window as the Felguard: "Doomguard (Ritual of Doom) ... Single-target plus utility (Cripple, War Stomp); one helper clicks" with a 30-minute cooldown, 15 with Master Summoner (guide/classes/warlock/demonology.md L136-L140, L148-L149).
- **WD0G3-inferno — Inferno:** HO-TKB-PLAY-276 (amp-3 draft rot-mage-warlock.patch of 2026-10-18, rebased by tkb-play onto main with HO-270..274; the amp-3 text follows): The Infernal, the one greater demon this file can use repeatedly: "Infernal (Inferno) ... Its punches are physical and go through dragon resistances" (guide/classes/warlock/demonology.md L136-L140).
- **WD00t-voidstone — Use Voidstone:** HO-TKB-PLAY-276 (amp-3 draft rot-mage-warlock.patch of 2026-10-18, rebased by tkb-play onto main with HO-270..274; the amp-3 text follows): Same stone pair as the affliction file, same reason: the guide gives the demonology lock the default "Felstone by default; Voidstone if threat is the problem" (guide/classes/warlock/affliction.md L236, the class-wide line) and the Voidstone is item 51936, on-use 52751, -11 threat for 30 minutes (rows L18607 and L27208). It sits above WD00t-felstone so a threat-capped demonology lock takes the threat stone and does not trade auras with it; `not aura_self(52751)` is the "already has this stone" term.
- **WD01c-summon-succubus — Summon Succubus:** HO-TKB-PLAY-276 (amp-3 draft rot-mage-warlock.patch of 2026-10-18, rebased by tkb-play onto main with HO-270..274; the amp-3 text follows with the tkb-play gate: Level 60 only: the levelling guide keeps the Voidwalker as the solo demon until 60 (leveling.md L205, L221, L244, L270); the Succubus and the Felhunter are the 60 choices of the spec page.): The missing Succubus, same shape as the affliction rule: the guide's level-20 line ("More damage than the Voidwalker but squishy. For demonology specifically the pet table prefers the Succubus once no greater demon is up when the group has melee buffs (guide/classes/warlock/demonology.md, Pets) and the Imp when it does not; with no predicate for either, the party case keeps the Imp rule and this one stays solo.
- **WD01e-summon-felhunter — Summon Felhunter:** HO-TKB-PLAY-276 (amp-3 draft rot-mage-warlock.patch of 2026-10-18, rebased by tkb-play onto main with HO-270..274; the amp-3 text follows with the tkb-play gate: Level 60 only: the levelling guide keeps the Voidwalker as the solo demon until 60 (leveling.md L205, L221, L244, L270); the Succubus and the Felhunter are the 60 choices of the spec page.): The Felhunter as the mana pet (guide: "Felhunter: mana regeneration" with the sacrifice table, affliction.md L180; destruction L182 "sacrifice the Felhunter instead of the Imp to Life Tap less"), level 30 at the kit and "~30 Felhunter" in the guide's level table (leveling.md L294), one Soul Shard. Fires only with no demon out and mana under 35 per cent, so it cannot displace the Imp in a party at healthy mana.
- **WD01-demon-armor — Demon Armor:** 30 mana, 30 min, armour and health regeneration; Demonic Aegis 3/3 in this build improves it, which is one of the few talents in this tree the rotation actually reads. HO-TKB-PLAY-013 (OQ-2568): out of combat this rule waits while the resident drinks or eats (aura 432, 433 or 435).
- **WD01d-summon-voidwalker-solo — Summon Voidwalker:** HO-TKB-PLAY-031 (orchestrator, round-47 delta-0 split): ALONE, from level 10, the Voidwalker is the levelling pet (guide: "Voidwalker, with Torment on autocast"; "Send the Voidwalker"; "the general leveling pet"). An Imp that is alive is not replaced: the pet predicates do not say which demon it is, so the Voidwalker comes when the Imp has died or been dismissed.
- **WD01a-summon-imp — Summon Imp:** THE WARLOCK HAD NO PET AT ALL, IN ANY OF ITS THREE ROTATIONS, AND A WARLOCK WITHOUT A DEMON IS NOT A WARLOCK. The Imp is the one this rule summons and the archive decides it, not preference: "every common-demon summon except Imp costs a Soul Shard", so the Imp is the only demon a bot can re-summon without a resource the vocabulary cannot see; the Voidwalker is explicitly not an answer -- "Attempting to use the demon as a tank: Voidwalker threat does not scale and consistently loses aggro even at higher character levels" -- and a dungeon party already has a warrior tank; and the Imp is the one that does damage at range (Firebolt) and carries Blood Pact for the party, which the archive prices by naming its loss a mistake ("Letting the Imp die to AoE and losing Blood Pact").
- **WD01b-health-funnel — Health Funnel:** 004 removed its Health Funnel because its only available guard was `not aura_self(6307)`, which is FALSE exactly while the Imp is alive and hurt -- the one state in which funnelling helps -- and TRUE while there is no pet to funnel to; from priority 14 that would have spent every in-combat tick above 70 per cent health. The reason is gone: `pet.exists`, `pet.alive` and `pet.hp_pct` are state-vocabulary v3 predicates implemented in Expr.cpp, so the rule can now ask the question it always needed to ask.
- **WD00s-caster-first-10499 — Shadow Bolt:** Its spell list (tkbplay-201.result.txt: 104990, Wail of Souls 17631, 7,580-8,059 hp, level 58-60) is instant and not interruptible per p4-group (spell_template: castingTimeIndex 1, interruptFlags 0; not re-read here), so no interrupt rule can answer it and killing it is the only kit answer; same shape and gates as the 10471 rule, just ahead of it.
- **WD02-life-tap — Life Tap:** Fel Intellect 3/3 and Fel Stamina 5/5 in this build make both bars bigger, which is the demonology way of saying the same thing. This rule carried NO combat gate, and out of combat that put it in a loop with the drink rule above it: WA00-drink is gated on `not aura_self(432)`, so once the drink aura is up the drink rule is FALSE and this rule takes the tick -- converting health to mana that the drink is already refilling for free.
- **WD00s-peel-11197 — Shadow Bolt:** Other Stratholme Undead adds are not sourced.
- **WD00s-caster-first-10471 — Shadow Bolt:** Mana Burn 17615 is instant and not interruptible (CastingTimeIndex 1, interruptFlags 0), so killing the caster is the only kit answer. amp-4's own count: the Acolyte/Neophyte pair is the killer in 149 of 263 deaths, but only 3 of 42 windows were kill-order-limited, so this is the orchestrator's ask, not the largest lever.
- **WD00s-caster-first-10470 — Shadow Bolt:** Mana Burn 17615 is instant and not interruptible (CastingTimeIndex 1, interruptFlags 0), so killing the caster is the only kit answer. amp-4's own count: the Acolyte/Neophyte pair is the killer in 149 of 263 deaths, but only 3 of 42 windows were kill-order-limited, so this is the orchestrator's ask, not the largest lever.
- **WD02a-pet-attack — pet attack:** HO-TKB-PLAY-048 (orchestrator, p4-group 123; HO-P4-GROUP-123 read round 79): send the pet at the resident's target once the fight is on, and again on a target change (pet.attacking is true only when the pet's victim is MY target). A defensive player pet ignores its owner's attack while it is out of combat (PetAI::OwnerAttacked returns when the pet is not in combat and its owner is a player), so with no rule that sends it in it fought only what hit it or its owner: on the tank's target on 84 of 169 in-combat ticks in round 79.
- **WD03-power-overwhelming — Power Overwhelming:** Turtle content and the spec's own cooldown: a Demonology talent (368), 80 mana, instant, 14 s recoveryTime, off the global cooldown, and its three aura effects make the demon larger, harder-hitting and, through a periodic percentage of its own health, shorter-lived. It is in the file with one guard missing and the note says which: v2 cannot ask whether there is a demon to empower (OQ-1809), so a push with none summoned is 80 mana for nothing and no rule here can prevent it.
- **WD04-shadow-ward — Shadow Ward:** HO-TKB-PLAY-013 (OQ-2568, OQ-2569): out of combat this rule waits while the resident drinks or eats (aura 432, 433 or 435). Once the eat rule stops re-pushing into its own aura, nothing else holds a self-defensive, a form, an aura or a mana cooldown back while seated, and any cast stands the resident up (Bots.DrinkHoldsUnlessHurt 0).
- **WD05-fear — Fear:** A demonology warlock has a demon holding the target, so this rule should fire less here than in either other file, and that is the point of the guard rather than an accident of it. Fear at under 35 per cent health is a way out of a fight that is being lost; against a mob at 30 per cent or less the way out is to finish it, which a DoT tick or one more bolt does while a Fear only gives it eight seconds to come back at full strength.
- **WD05b-curse-of-recklessness — Curse of Recklessness:** HO-TKB-PLAY-276 (amp-3 draft rot-mage-warlock.patch of 2026-10-18, rebased by tkb-play onto main with HO-270..274; the amp-3 text follows with the tkb-play gate: level 60 only: Malediction (the Recklessness trick) is an affliction talent and the demonology path keeps Curse of Agony below 60 (leveling.md L166, L199)): THE DEMONOLOGY CURSE, and it is Recklessness rather than Shadows for a reason the guide states: "Curse missing -> curse. When you are free to choose, use Curse of Recklessness: greater demons deal physical damage, and it also helps the tank's threat" (guide/classes/warlock/demonology.md, single-target priority 4).
- **WD06-curse-of-agony — Curse of Agony:** The one curse this file keeps up.
- **WD07a-rain-of-fire — Rain of Fire:** THE DEMONOLOGY FILE HAD NO MULTI-TARGET RULE AT ALL. Rain of Fire is a level-20 trainer spell in the generated warlock kit, available to every spec, and was absent from the affliction and demonology rotations entirely.
- **WD04b-fear-second — Fear:** HO-TKB-PLAY-038 (orchestrator; p1-loop v12 answers OQ-2817): Fear (5782, level 8, 15 per cent of base mana, 1.5 s, 20 yd) on the OTHER attacker, after the DoTs: this rule sits below Agony, Corruption and Immolate, so the kill target carries them first, which is the guide''s order ("DoT both, then Fear the one that is not on you", "Fear B after its DoTs are on", "Fear breaks on new spell applications, not on DoT ticks, so DoT BEFORE you Fear"). The spell has no creature-type mask; a fear-immune creature takes two casts and is then skipped for ten seconds.
- **WD10f-drain-soul-finisher — Drain Soul:** HO-TKB-PLAY-346 (amp-5 review of HO-330, the shard budget; leveling.md L186, L282, L283): Drain Soul on a dying non-boss target, so the warlock gets Soul Shards back the way a human does (finish with Drain Soul when you need shards). Why it is needed: the Soul Shard stacks to 3 (DB item 6265) and the kit carries a stack count agreed with p4-pioneer (2 stacks, 6 shards, for destruction and affliction, 1 stack, 3, for demonology; p4-pioneer change, before the 23:00 CEST regeneration; dropped to one stack if this finisher makes the second unnecessary after a round).
- **WD09-drain-life — Drain Life:** HO-TKB-PLAY-274 (leveller pass; guide leveling.md L199, L321): the Demonology levelling loop is the Voidwalker, the DoTs, then Drain Life or the wand; it is not Shadow Bolt.
- **WD11w-shoot-trash — Shoot:** HO-TKB-PLAY-065 (owner approved, via the orchestrator: wand earlier on trash, keep the full spells for bosses and big pulls; the warlock ended 10 of 56 round-86 fights under 20 per cent mana): the wand instead of the filler when the target is under 30 per cent health, or the warlock is under 40 per cent mana, in a fight that is not a boss or a big pull (`not (target.ttd_ms >= 15000)`: a target that will take 15 s or more is a long fight, null reads true; `enemies_engaged_within(30) <= 3`: four or more keep the spells; `party.pull_is_boss` is true only while a pull is imminent).
- **WD10a-wand-solo — Shoot:** The guide for 4-9: "Corruption -> Immolate -> wand", from 8 "Curse of Agony -> Corruption -> wand"; and the bot-ready loop: "Nightfall proc -> Shadow Bolt. In a party nothing changes (`not (party.lowest_hp_pct >= 0)` is the solo test the rogue Stealth rule uses).
- **WD10-shadow-bolt — Shadow Bolt:** 25 mana at rank 1, a 1700 ms cast, 30 yd, and Unholy Power 3/3 and Master Demonologist 5/5 in this build are both about the demon rather than about this.
- **WD11-shoot — Shoot:** Measured on d-20260917T070130Z-p3, actor 358: the wand was 26 per cent of the mage''s casts, 86 per cent of its starts were unasked, 7 ticks were wand-locked, and 35 of its own casts came back SPELL_FAILED_INTERRUPTED -- the bot''s own movement cancelling its own auto-repeat. `not self.moving` is the other half and is the 35 interrupted casts: a wand shot the bot walks out of is a lock bought for nothing.
